transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I came in because... well, I've been having trouble talking to people lately. I'm a jeweler, and when a customer asks me a simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready, I just can't seem to give them a straight answer. My mind just kind of wanders. I'll start talking about their invoice, and then somehow that makes me think about garden soil, and then suddenly I'm talking about my mortgage papers. I can see the look on their faces, I can see them losing me, but I just can't seem to keep my thoughts straight.
About how long have you been noticing this trouble with your thoughts jumping around?

Well, the trouble with my thoughts jumping around... I guess it all started around a year and eight months ago. That's also when I started hearing the voices, noticing those strange smells, and feeling worried that the customers were watching us.
During this year and eight months, have you experienced any periods where you felt deeply depressed or persistently down?

Yes, I have. Um, most mornings, actually, I wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. It's just there. It feels like the color has completely drained out of the house before I even get to the shop for the day.
Have there been times during this past year and eight months when you heard the voices or felt watched, but were not feeling sad or depressed?

Yes, there was. Um, there was a stretch before the depression really settled in where I felt okay. I was actually still running my jewelry classes and keeping up with my gardening. But even then, for several weeks, I kept hearing noises coming from the polishing room, and I was already worrying that customers were watching the business. So, yes, those things were happening even before the sadness started.
Looking back over that year and eight months, about how much of that total time have you felt that heavy sadness?

Well, the heavy sadness... I'd say it's been with me for about a year and four months now. It really started during that long stretch when the pressure of the mortgage just started feeling completely impossible to handle.
